items.title: A derived limit of a compatible system of pseudo-coherent objects over surjective ring maps is pseudo-coherent
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The statement concerns an inverse system of rings with surjective transition maps having locally nilpotent kernels, objects over each ring compatible under reduction, and asks that the derived limit be pseudo-coherent and be recovered by reduction (statement lines 28335-28351). The proof represents the first object by a bounded above complex of finite free modules, propagates pseudo-coherence along the system through the nilpotent kernel statement, lifts the system to complexes of finite free modules whose reductions are isomorphisms of complexes, and then identifies the derived limit with the limit complex, whose terms are finite free of the same bounded ranks (proof lines 28353-28374). The strictness of the reductions is what makes the limit complex computable and hence pseudo-coherent. The counted span refers five times, four times to results of this chapter and once to a remark of this chapter accompanying the computation of derived limits, all carried as navigation stubs.
